brief: #137 swept every population cap and found the one it could not raise: `laneCap` has NO knee up to 19. It buys people linearly because each of the plaza, quay, far green, parapet and allotment-detour destinations is only 5-6% of one `spawnLaneAgent` roll, so past 10 every marginal arrival is a lane walker and the east half stays flat (plaza presence 4.84 -> 4.68 -> 4.71 as the cap climbs). The branch SHARE, not the ceiling, is what bounds the east. Re-weight the roll so raising the cap actually reaches the east. Fold in its twin: the plaza has three FAMILY places and only two are reserved - `famBench` locks a bench, the 1.6-cell fountain strip locks nothing - so `FAM_CAP` saturates at 3 and going higher doubles crowded pairs instead of adding families. Reserve the stand, then re-sweep FAM_CAP. Why now: lane is 4 back, both premises are #137's own measurements, and the east half of every wide shot is visibly thinner than the courtyard.
successLooksLike: Presence per PLACE (probes/town-caps.mjs is the instrument) shows the plaza, quay and far green rising with the cap where they were flat, and the lane not collapsing. FAM_CAP raised above 3 with crowded pairs PER PERSON flat, not merely with more families on screen. Same pinned instant, same seed: the east half of the wide shot is fuller.
avoid: Do not raise `laneCap` again - #137 already swept it and the ceiling is not the bound. Do not give the east its own new arrival source; the WATCH note says to check whether a feature needs one, and here the answer is no, the roll exists and is mis-weighted. Two figures nearer than ~0.9 cells render as one shape, so a reserved fountain stand needs PAIR_GAP of clearance for a family, not just legal ground.
